**Subject: Knocknacarra Tuesday club – improved attendance, and something I should have checked with you**

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, because there has been a real change in the Tuesday reading club since your email of 30 October. You proposed pausing it from January because of the low attendance and the increase in the hall insurance. I understand the insurance difficulty has not gone away, and I don’t want to gloss over that, but I do hope the attendance figures might now give us reason to reconsider the pause.

The club has been running since September, on Tuesdays from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library. We had five children most weeks in September. By mid-October that had risen to nine, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen children. I am thrilled, not just by the numbers but by what is happening among them.

Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another boy, who would hardly open a book in September, asked last week whether he could take two home with him. Moments like those tell me that the children are beginning to feel at home with books, which is what we were hoping for all along.

We have also had wonderful support from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook, who donated 120 books. Most are suitable for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. They have made a real difference to what we can offer.

After such a slow start, it feels as though the club has genuinely taken off. Pausing it in January would be a terrible pity just at that point. Could I ask you to look at these new figures before the meeting on the 18th and reconsider the proposed pause? I would very much welcome the chance to discuss the practical difficulties, including the insurance, rather than lose the momentum now.

There is also something I need to tell you myself, because I did not handle it properly. I met Orla Keane, a reporter with the Corrib Courier, at the farmers’ market. I got carried away telling her how well the club was going and said, “Come along any Tuesday.” She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I should have checked with you before saying anything of the sort. I was wrong not to check first, plain and simple, and I certainly do not want to present you with a visit as a fait accompli. I know the policy clearly: no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms.

I think local coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it is done properly, with your agreement and on whatever terms you set. I can ring Orla immediately and put the visit on hold until you have decided. If you are agreeable in principle, I am very happy to collect the parental consent forms myself and make sure everything is in place beforehand. If you would prefer that the visit not go ahead, I will explain that to her.

I am sorry for creating this extra bother, but I would much rather you heard it directly from me. My main hope is that the children’s progress and the recent growth in attendance can be given proper weight at the review. A great deal has changed since September, and I think we now have something well worth keeping going.

Kind regards,  
[Your name]
